about.title: About me
paragraphs: I recently graduated as a Bachelor of Science and am now continuing in the master's programme at Tampere University, majoring in communications engineering with a minor in economics.

Outside of tech I love all kinds of handcraft, from knitting to wood carving. My most unique skill is probably traditional Karelian embroidery: the precise stitching and careful pattern-making hooked me the first time I tried it.
This site is where those two sides meet.

embroidery.description: A free web tool for drafting Karelian embroidery patterns on a stitch grid and downloading them as PDF.
embroidery.title: Karelian Embroidery Designer
embroidery.lead: A web tool for drafting Karelian embroidery patterns, because graph paper only gets you so far.
embroidery.ctaNote: Free, and runs in your browser
embroidery.photoAlt: An embroidered bookmark: white Karelian-style birds and spirals stitched on blue fabric
embroidery.photoCaption: Birds and spirals: a bookmark I embroidered.
story: The idea came from my own embroidery. When I started drafting my own patterns, I quickly noticed that there were no ready-made tools for Karelian embroidery pattern-making.
Drafting on paper is quick and easy, of course, but I wanted a way to catalogue the patterns and motifs that are used again and again in Karelian embroidery.
embroidery.screenshotAlt: Screenshot of the Karelian Embroidery Designer: a toolbar of stitch tools above a grid with a bird motif drawn in red
features: Draw on a stitch grid with straight, diagonal and cross stitches
Set the width and height of the pattern
Undo mistakes or start over with a clean grid
Download the finished pattern as a PDF
planned: Templates of traditional motifs to start from
Saving your own motifs as templates
embroidery.tradition: Karelian embroidery is a traditional counted-thread technique from Karelia. The stitches follow the threads of an even-weave fabric and build up geometric motifs: rhombuses, crosses, branches and birds, traditionally in red on white linen.
embroidery.closingTitle: Ready to draft your own pattern?
